question: A cylindrical rod has an outer curved surface area of 7500 cm² . If the length of the rod is 87 cm, then the outer radius (in cm) of the rod, correct to two places of decimal, is: (Take pi=(22)/(7))
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The outer radius of a cylinder can be found directly using the Curved Surface Area (CSA) formula.

r = CSA ÷ (2 × π × h)

⇒ r = 7500 × 7 ÷ (2 × 22 × 87)

⇒ r = 52500 ÷ 3828

⇒ r ≈ 13.71 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13.71 cm.**

**Given:**

Curved surface area (CSA) of the cylinder = 7500 cm²

Length (height, h) of the cylinder = 87 cm

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of a cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 87 = 7500

⇒ (44/7) × 87 × r = 7500

⇒ (3828/7) × r = 7500

⇒ r = 7500 × 7 ÷ 3828

⇒ r = 52500 ÷ 3828

⇒ r ≈ 13.714... cm

⇒ r ≈ 13.71 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13.71 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cylinder

It is the area of the curved surface, excluding the top and bottom circular bases. Formula: CSA = 2πrh

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

It includes the curved surface area plus the areas of the two circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πr(r + h)

Volume of a Cylinder

It measures the total three-dimensional space enclosed by the cylinder. Formula: V = πr²h
